outlooks.summary: The greatest severe-thunderstorm potential through tonight will be over portions of North Dakota and northwestern Minnesota, with damaging gusts and hail being the greatest threats.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, an elongated/positively tilted anticyclone -- centered over the central High Plains -- will dominate the pattern over central North America through the period. The ridge extending northeastward from the associated 500-mb high is expected to shift eastward from MB to northwestern ON, and from the eastern Dakotas across MN. This will occur as a strong shortwave trough -- initially evident in moisture-channel imagery as a weak/closed cyclone over the Canadian Rockies -- will become open-wave in nature and reach eastern SK by 12Z. Meanwhile, east of the synoptic ridge, a compact mid/upper-level cyclone was apparent over the eastern James Bay region, and is forecast to dig south-southeastward toward northern NY by the end of the period. Farther southwest, a broad, weak cut-off cyclone -- containing several embedded vorticity maxima and a mix of warm- and cold-core characteristics -- was located over the lower Mississippi Valley. This feature should continue to move slowly southwestward to portions of south-central/southeast TX through tomorrow morning. sections.title: Northern Plains/Upper Midwest
sections.text: An ongoing complex of strong-severe thunderstorms will post a threat for sporadic damaging winds and isolated hail as it moves eastward to southeastward through the remainder of the morning. Activity largely should follow an elevated (850-mb) theta-e gradient corresponding to the low-level warm-frontal zone, eventually weakening as it moves away from the axis of a low-level jet over central ND. See SPC watch 460 and related mesoscale discussions for near-term guidance on this activity. The "Enhanced"/30% wind probabilities represent a composite threat from the morning MCS and the second round of convection this afternoon/evening. The morning complex should lay down an outflow boundary across eastern/central ND that will reinforce the surface warm-frontal zone and perhaps impede its northward movement prior to the next round of convection, forecast to form largely along the cold front this afternoon and evening. Low-level shear, convergence, storm-relative flow and vorticity all should be relatively maximized near the triple point where the front overtakes the outflow boundary. sections.title: Northeastern CONUS
sections.text: Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop from midday through early evening across the western and northern parts of the outlook area and move southeastward, offering sporadic damaging to severe gusts and occasional, mostly marginally severe hail. The wind threat should extend farther south than that for severe hail, given the tendency for convection to aggregate more upscale with time and evolve into at least loosely organized/broken bands. The preconvective air mass across the region will be weakly capped and destabilizing throughout the day. Buoyancy generally will increase southward, in keeping with grater low-level moisture and longer-lasting episodes of direct sunshine/heating. Peak MLCAPE should range from around 500-1000 J/kg over northern NY and New England, and 1500-2500 J/kg from portions of NJ across southeastern New England. Well-mixed subcloud layers with steep lapse rates are expected, contributing to the convective-wind potential. Ambient boundary-layer flow should remain modest, and the deep-layer wind profiles should be nearly unidirectional, only minor veering with height being likely. outlooks.summary: The greatest severe thunderstorm potential through tonight will be across parts of the eastern Dakotas and western Minnesota. Tornadoes, large hail, and damaging winds are possible.

sections.title: Upper Midwest
sections.text: A weakening linear cluster is ongoing across east-central ND with an associated MCV over northeast ND. Potential exists for this cluster to persist along the pronounced MLCAPE gradient that extends southeast across western MN. However, strong MLCIN may be sufficient to further weaken this lead MCS during the early to mid afternoon. Renewed thunderstorm development is anticipated towards early evening in parts of central to eastern ND as convergence along the residual outflow boundary/cold front overcomes weakness in MLCIN. Once storms fire, they should rapidly intensify given the presence an extremely unstable air mass (MLCAPE >4000 J/kg) amid very steep mid-level lapse rates around 9 C/km and a plume of low to mid 70s surface dew points. Most convection will probably develop towards the cool side of the remnant outflow boundary given the strength of the warm-sector EML. Uncertainty exists in the degree of recovery to the northeast as morning guidance has generally poorly handled the southern extent and persistence of the lead MCS with its related stabilizing effects in its immediate wake. sections.title: Mid-Atlantic/Northeast States
sections.text: Scattered convection is ongoing across western/central PA and this activity should intensify through the afternoon as the greatest insolation is underway across central/eastern PA to NJ and south. While mid-level lapse rates will remain moderate and more importantly, effective shear values only reach around 20-30 kts, the moderately unstable air mass will encourage multicell clusters with damaging winds from strong gusts as the primary threat into early evening. More isolated thunderstorm coverage is expected farther north in western New England owing to abundant cloudiness yielding weaker instability at peak heating. However, multiple rounds of convection are anticipated, with a later round tonight as large-scale ascent strengthens with approach of a shortwave trough digging from James bay across southwest Quebec.

sections.title: Central/East TX
sections.text: A weak mid-level low over the Sabine Valley should drift southwest across southeast TX. A narrow belt of enhanced mid-level northerlies to the northwest of the circulation may aid in weakly organized multicell clustering as ongoing convection likely intensifies as it spreads southwest this afternoon and evening. Locally damaging winds and marginal hail are the anticipated hazards. ..Grams/Karstens.. 06/29/2019

outlooks.summary: The greatest severe thunderstorm potential through tonight will be across central through eastern North Dakota into western Minnesota. Large hail, damaging winds as well as a few tornadoes are possible.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Primary change to previous outlook has been to adjust ENH risk area farther NW into central and eastern ND and western MN. Expansive outflow boundary from dying MCS extends from central MN westward to a weak surface low over northwest SD. This boundary should stall and begin to advance slowly northward this afternoon, and the surface layer should destabilize through central and eastern ND through the evening. Although some uncertainty still persists, storms are expected to initiate by early evening across central ND, possibly at the intersection of northward-advancing outflow boundary and cold front. Initial storms will be supercells, and low-level hodographs near the modifying outflow boundary will be sufficient for low-level mesocyclones and a tornado threat. Otherwise large hail appears likely before storms consolidate into an MCS and continue east and southeast later into the evening and overnight with a predominant damaging wind threat. ..Dial.. 06/29/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1135 AM CDT Sat Jun 29 2019/

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of large hail, damaging winds as well as a few tornadoes are possible this evening over North Dakota. The severe risk will transition to damaging winds overnight from parts of the Dakotas into the Upper Midwest.

sections.title: Northern Great Plains and Upper Midwest
sections.text: The glancing of a Saskatchewan mid-level shortwave trough this evening will favor additional storm development over parts of the Dakotas this evening as a southerly LLJ strengthens before veering overnight. A very moisture-rich/unstable airmass was sampled this evening by the 00z Bismarck and Aberdeen raobs with deep-layer shear considerably less with south extent across the Dakotas. The greatest risk for supercell-related severe hazards (tornado, hail, wind) will likely focus this evening over ND. Additional storms are forecast by late evening into the overnight near and north of earlier-day convective outflow along the effective warm frontal zone. The transition to primarily a damaging wind threat will accompany storms as they grow upscale later tonight.

sections.title: Northeast into the Mid-Atlantic states
sections.text: A vigorous mid-level low southeast of James Bay will move southeast tonight. As the boundary layer cools this evening, the propensity for strong to locally severe gusts will likely diminish across the Mid-Atlantic states and become increasingly confined across parts of the Northeast. A perhaps amplified risk for damaging gusts may continue for the next hour across northern NY into VT but the small spatiotemporal character of the threat will preclude the introduction of higher probabilities.

sections.title: Parts of central TX
sections.text: A few clusters of storms moving south-southwest from near the Metroplex and east-central TX will probably continue for the next few hours. The strongest outflow and cores may be capable of an isolated severe threat into the mid evening hours. ..Smith.. 06/30/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will spread across eastern portions of ww460 by 1630z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Well-organized MCS is maturing over north-central ND, an upscale continuation of eastern MT convection late Friday. Within the MCS, an MCV is now evident north of DVL. Leading edge of strong convection is moving southeast at roughly 35kt. Given this speed, severe threat should spread to near the MN border between 16-1630z. Wind, and some hail, remain the primary risks with this activity. ..Darrow.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Locally damaging winds can be expected with thunderstorms this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong boundary-layer heating across central PA into south-central NY is contributing to steep low-level lapse rates. Latest diagnostic data suggests surface-3km values are now approaching 8 C/km and convective temperatures will soon be breached as surface readings rise through the mid 80s. Deepening boundary-layer cu across western/central NY reflect larger height falls that are spreading south and isolated thunderstorms are now increasing across western PA. Scattered robust convection is expected to mature and spread/develop into southern New England and the northern Middle Atlantic region. Strong winds and some hail are possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Squall line will progress across the remainder of ww460 into northwest MN over the next hour. Locally strong winds are the primary threat. New ww is not currently anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Squall line continues its movement southeast at roughly 35kt and will soon spread east of ww460 into northwest MN. Majority of measured wind gusts are less than 45kt ahead of this activity and hail algorithm suggests hail sizes are less than 1". Unless this convection begins to intensify, current thinking is to not issue another watch downstream. ..Darrow.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat continues across much of ww461.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early-day convection that developed in the lee of Lake Erie has gradually evolved into an elongated, arcing squall line from central PA to near the OH border. Leading edge of this convection is surging southeast at 25-30kt and would approach the western portions of PHL metro by 2030-21z. Of some concern is the southern flank which will approach the MD border in the next hour or so. This activity could spread south of ww461 into northeast MD with the southern-most extent possibly extending into the Delmarva. ..Darrow.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated wind/hail threat, watch not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regional radar trends over the past hour show a few pulse storms that have developed over portions of southeastern Oklahoma and eastern Texas, moving west-southwest and have mostly remained sub-severe. These storms are moving into a north-south oriented instability axis characterized by MLCAPE of 2500-3000 J/kg. This convective activity is occurring on the the western periphery of a weak mid/upper-level retrograding low, where some marginally enhanced mid-level flow is present, yielding perhaps 30 kt of effective bulk shear. Throughout the remainder of the afternoon and evening, additional storms should continue to develop. Despite relatively marginal mid-level lapse rates, steep low-level lapse rates (near 8 C/km) will promote a threat for isolated strong outflow winds along with an isolated hail threat given the aforementioned instability. The latest convection-allowing guidance suggests a few small clusters of storms may emerge. However, the threat for damaging winds and hail is expected to remain mostly localized/transient, and thus a watch is not expected at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Primary severe risk is shifting into the NJ and adjacent Delmarva region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Long-lived cluster of convection continues its southeast movement across PA and is spreading into NJ and adjacent regions of northern DE/VA. This activity is producing locally damaging wind gusts with 42kt measured at KLVJ at 1951z. Numerous discrete cells have recently developed ahead of the main line across NJ and this may bleed off some buoyancy ahead of the squall line. Even so, damaging winds appear to be the main threat. ..Darrow.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: It remains unclear how much longer isolated supercell development will persist over parts of southwestern South Dakota. It still seems unlikely that a severe weather watch will be needed, but trends will continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The isolated supercell, which initiated around 20Z, appeared to do so as somewhat cooler air surged southeast of the Black Hills and locally enhanced convergence within lee surface troughing to the south of the Badlands. Along the axis of strongest surface heating and deep boundary layer mixing, temperatures are near 100F, with CAPE a relatively modest 1500-2000 J/kg. The storm appears embedded within generally light southwesterly deep layer mean flow, but substantial veering of winds with height is contributing to at least modest deep layer mean shear. Still, due substantial mid-level inhibition associated with a broad plume of very warm elevated mixed-layer air, and generally lack of appreciable large-scale forcing for upward vertical motion, it remains unclear how much longer this cell will persist.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms will cross the US-Canadian border in the next hour or two into Upstate New York and northern New England. Strong wind gusts and large hail are possible, but a watch issuance is unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have formed along/ahead a cold front pushing through southeast Canada and will move into Upstate New York and northern New England in the next hour or two. A warm, moist airmass with surface temperatures in the upper 70s to low 80s F and dewpoints in the 60s F has resulted in MLCAPE of 1000+ J/kg. Strong mid-level flow associated with the upper-level trough over Quebec has resulted in unidirectional speed shear with long hodographs across the region that could result in some weaker supercells, with the potential for isolated large hail. Isolated strong/severe winds are also possible given the relatively steep low-level lapse rates (8+ C/km). However, overall, the severe wind/hail threat is marginal and since storms will weaken after sunset, a watch issuance is unlikely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The potential for sustained thunderstorm development across the region remains unclear into early evening. But, any storms that do form will pose a risk for severe hail, perhaps a tornado, and eventually locally strong surface gusts. While it is not certain that a severe weather watch will be needed, trends will continue to be monitored for this possibility.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: There appear at least attempts at scattered sustained thunderstorm initiation ongoing across the region, generally focused along a remnant outflow boundary/zone of stronger differential surface heating, and within the lee surface troughing. This may be in response to forcing for ascent associated with locally enhanced low-level convergence, and broader low-level warm advection, aided by 20-30+ kt southerly 850 mb flow along and east of the surface trough. However, it is also within/beneath a broad plume of very warm elevated mixed-layer air, which is contributing to substantial inhibition. And, mid/upper support for large-scale ascent appears weak. Still, a combination of seasonably high boundary layer moisture, particularly along the zone of stronger differential surface heating, is contributing to large CAPE, probably well in excess of 4000 J/kg. This provides potential for rapid thunderstorm development and intensification, in an environment where veering of wind profiles with height beneath westerly mid/upper flow is contributing to sufficient shear for supercells. If lift becomes sufficient to support sustained deep convection late this afternoon, storms probably will pose at least some risk for severe hail, perhaps a tornado, and eventually strong surface gusts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong/severe storms will likely continue moving south-southeast across central PA and into eastern PA this evening. Large hail and strong winds remain the main threats and a local watch extension may be necessary.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have redeveloped across western/northern PA behind the initial line of storms that moved through central/eastern PA this afternoon. Storms have mostly moved through an area that was not convectively overturned earlier in the day or had enough time to recover with daytime heating resulting in MLCAPE of 1000-1500+ J/kg. The airmass remains unstable just to the south/east of the current line of storms, but farther east/south into Pennsylvania and New Jersey, the airmass has mostly stabilized. These storms are moving just south of the best mid-level flow, but sufficient shear remains to support strong to severe storms. Severe hail/wind remain possible with these storms, especially if any localized bowing segments can form with a stronger cold pool behind it. Given the current storm motion/trajectory, a local watch extension may be necessary for portions of eastern/southern PA. However, redevelopment behind the current storms is unlikely and storms are likely to weaken after sunset helping to limit the severe threat beyond 23-00z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Evolving supercellular convection probably will pose increasing risk for severe hail, and potential for tornadoes, through 9-10 PM near/south of Bismarck.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Considerable inhibition evident in 30/00Z raob from Bismarck probably has contributed to slow intensification of convection. However, attempts at vigorous convective development persist along the zone of stronger differential surface heating, where seasonably high boundary layer moisture content (surface dew points in the lower 70s) is contributing to large mixed-layer CAPE in excess of 4000 J/kg. With only slow boundary-layer cooling likely during the next several hours, the environment will remain favorable for considerable intensification, in the presence of strongly sheared 30+ kt southwesterly deep-layer ambient mean flow. Recent trends evident in observational data suggest that this may already be underway to the southwest of Bismarck. As this activity continues eastward, near and to the south of Bismarck between now and 02-03Z, it will begin to encounter stronger southerly 850 mb flow of 20-30+ kt. As it does, larger clockwise curved low-level hodographs may become supportive of a period of increasing potential for tornadoes, before beginning to grow upscale and transitioning to more of a severe wind threat, in addition to large hail. ..Kerr.. 06/30/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Increasing thunderstorm development posing at least a risk for severe hail is possible late this evening, with the gradual evolution of an organized cluster of storms possible by Midnight-1 AM CDT. The issuance of a severe weather watch probably will hinge on the consolidation of storms into an organizing cluster that may pose an increasing risk for strong wind gusts later tonight.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As a significant short wave trough shifts east-northeastward across the Canadian Prairies this evening, some suppression of downstream mid-level ridging is underway near the North Dakota/Minnesota international border area. In lower-levels, a modest southerly low-level jet (30-35 kt at 850 mb) across eastern portions of the northern Plains will gradually veer to a more southwesterly component late this evening into the overnight hours. Strongest lower/mid tropospheric warm advection associated with this jet is currently focused north of the eastern North/South Dakota border area through much of northeastern North Dakota and northwest Minnesota. Associated sustained lift of moist air characterized by large CAPE in the presence of steep mid-level lapse rates may begin to overcome inhibition associated with warm elevated mixed-layer within the next few hours. Thunderstorm activity is already initiating near the international border area, with additional development most probable within the thermal gradient around 700 mb, across northeastern North Dakota into northwest Minnesota. However, at least some southward suppression of the warmer mid-level air may allow thunderstorm initiation as far south as the Interstate-94 corridor. As storms develop, stronger cells may become capable of producing severe hail in the presence of strong deep layer shear, with a gradual consolidation and upscale growth possible through 05-06Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for severe weather has diminished in the near term, but new storm development appears possible near and north of the Interstate 94 corridor east of Bismarck by 11 PM-1 AM CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: After a period of substantive intensification, the influence of substantial mid-level inhibition has resulted in the dissipation of the supercell southwest through south of Bismarck. The potential for additional storm development rooted within the strongly unstable boundary layer in close proximity to the remnant zone of stronger differential surface heating appears low. However, there still appears potential for storm initiation, including supercells, rooted within the low-level warm advection regime across much of eastern North Dakota within the next few hours (as discussed further in MCD 1308). This could include at least northeastern portions of Tornado Watch 463 prior to its scheduled 06Z expiration. ..Kerr.. 06/30/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for marginally severe wind or hail continues across the watch area. A few strong elevated storms may persist into northwest Wisconsin, but additional watches are not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An MCS continues to move generally southeastward across northern MN, on the nose of a low-level theta-e plume and with isentropic lift aided by a 30 kt low-level jet. The primary cold-pool surge is moving across Itasca County, and will continue into St. Louis County. Surface observations show a relatively cool air mass east of the warm front, and as such several sub-severe wind gusts have been measured. Since it is unlikely that the instability gradient moves much eastward, additional downstream watches are unlikely in the near term. Along the southwestern flank of this MCS, storm cores may periodically become capable of marginal hail with better access to unstable air. Otherwise, storms may eventually drop south/southeast along the instability gradient, with marginally severe wind also possible. ..Jewell.. 06/30/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A line of storms will continue to move south/southeast into central Minnesota and western Wisconsin, with at least isolated severe wind gusts possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A line of storms currently extends from Duluth westward to Cass County and has begun to bow southward. This trajectory will keep western parts of the line close to the instability gradient which is oriented north-south, with the warm/moist influx coming from the west. Recently, a severe wind gust was measured at KAIT, suggesting this MCS is gaining access to the better instability. As such, a watch may be needed if trends persist.
